newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Deve Gowda moves vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: India's Deve Gowda moves vote of confidence.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Friday moved a vote of confidence in his government before the lower house of parliament.

"I would like to move the vote of confidence," Deve Gowda told the 542-member lower house, the Lok Sabha, which convened in a special sitting. The vote was expected to be held after 8 p.m. (1430 GMT) on Friday.
The motion read: "That this House expresses its confidence in the Council of Ministers."
President Shankar Dayal Sharma asked Deve Gowda to call the confidence vote after the Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support for the prime minister's minority coalition government.
Deve Gowda's chances of surviving the vote appeared thin. His United Front coalition controls 178 votes in the Lok Sabha.

Congress on Thursday ordered its 140 deputies to vote against the motion. On Friday morning, the rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its allies, with 193 votes, decided to vote against Deve Gowda.
